requirement:
A result of the `habeas` line-range form, `list_files`, `outline`, `ripgrep`,
`ast_grep`, or `references` whose serialized JSON exceeds 32 KiB MUST be
returned in pages. Each page MUST hold whole entries of the result's arrays, such
as inputs, matches, nodes, or sites, with its accompanying definitions, in the
result's order, and MUST NOT exceed 32 KiB unless a single entry does, which
then forms a page of its own. Every paged result MUST include:

```text
page: {
    total_entries: Integer,
    returned_entries: Integer,
    next: String?,
}
```

`next` MUST be an opaque token when entries remain and null on the last page. The
harness MUST expose a `next_page({ token: String })` tool returning the following
page of the same result, in the same shape. Pages MUST be kept only until the
assessment that requested them finishes; an unknown token, including one from
another assessment, MUST return an explanatory tool error. A result within the
limit MUST be returned whole, without `page`. Only inputs on pages delivered to
the model MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every obligation has marked implementing code and a test that runs it.

**Obligations and their code**
- **Paging above 32 KiB, whole below it.** `PAGE_LIMIT` is 32 KiB (`pages.rs`). `ResultPages::deliver` renders the whole result and returns it unchanged, with no `page` field, when its JSON is at most the limit. Otherwise it pages the result. All six paged tools reach this through `tools::dispatch_paged`: `habeas` line-range via `read` → `Listing::inputs`, plus `list_files`, `outline`, `ripgrep`, `ast_grep` (including `declared_query`) and `references`. The item, requirements and definition forms of `habeas`, and `github`, are not paged, as the text requires.
- **Whole entries, in the result's order, with accompanying definitions.**
  - `Listing` keeps each entry together with its array index.
  - `paginate` produces consecutive ranges of whole entries.
  - `definitions_each` and `page_definitions` attach each page's own definitions.
  - `render` builds the page under the proper array keys, or under `entries` for bare arrays.
- **Page size.** `paginate` counts sizes from above (a comma per element, plus accompanying definitions and the longest possible `page` object). It starts a new page before any overflow. An entry that alone exceeds the limit forms its own one-entry page.
- **`page` object.** `deliver` emits `total_entries`, `returned_entries` and `next` on each page.
- **`next` token.** `next` is a 16-hex-character random token, unique within `ResultPages`, from `ResultPages::token`. It is null on the last page, because `tokens.get(number)` returns `None` there.
- **`next_page` tool.** It is advertised in `tools::definitions` and dispatched in `dispatch_paged`. `ResultPages::next_page` returns the stored page, which has the same shape as the first.
- **Per-assessment storage and unknown tokens.** `converse` creates a fresh `ResultPages` for each assessment, so tokens from another assessment are unknown. An unknown token returns an explanatory `io::Error`, and `converse` turns it into a tool error result.
- **Delivered inputs.** `deliver` returns only the current page's inputs and definitions in `ToolDelivery.inputs`. `converse` records them via `pending` and `record_inputs`. Later pages are recorded only when requested through `next_page`.

**Tests**
- `pages.rs`
  - `large_listings_and_outlines_page_whole_entries_in_order` covers `list_files` and `outline`. It checks the size limit, order, no duplicates, `returned_entries` counts, and null `next` on the last page via `all_pages`.
  - `paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs` covers `ripgrep` paging, per-page definitions, and delivered inputs equal to the page's inputs plus its definitions. It also checks an unknown token from another assessment, a bogus token through `dispatch_paged`, and re-fetching a page.
  - `an_entry_exceeding_the_limit_forms_a_page_of_its_own_and_small_results_stay_whole` covers the line-range `habeas` form, the oversize single-entry page, and whole results with no `page` field.
  - `reference_results_page_definitions_then_sites` covers `references` paging, with definitions before sites and a combined total of 800.
- `mod.rs`: `only_inputs_on_delivered_pages_are_recorded` runs an end-to-end conversation with `next_page`. It asserts that only inputs from delivered pages appear in the evidence.
- `tools.rs`: `next_page_is_advertised_and_paged_tools_explain_their_pages` checks that the `next_page` tool and the paging notes are advertised.

`ast_grep` has no paging test of its own. It uses the same `Listing::inputs` and `deliver` path as `ripgrep`, so it has no separate path that needs one.

**Marking.** The implementing items I read carry `{impl}` references to `result_pages`, and the tests carry `{test}` references. I found no unmarked implementing code and no unspecified behavior.
